tool_input.command:
cd <repo>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(hooks): resolve push-guard branch where the push invocation runs, not just payload cwd

F5 (MEDIUM, from background security review): the branch check
resolved the current branch from the hook payload's own cwd, but a
push invocation can redirect where it actually runs -- `git -C
<dir> push` or a preceding `cd <dir> &&` both move the invocation
somewhere other than cwd. `git -C /some/repo push origin feat` from a
feature-worktree cwd checked the worktree's branch while the push
itself ran, and could push, from /some/repo. This gap predates this
mission (the pre-mission hook had the same blind spot via
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) but sits squarely in this hook's write set.

Fixed by resolving a "scope" from the push invocation's own text before
checking the branch: the last `-C <dir>` on the git invocation (git's
own semantics -- each -C is relative to the previous one, so only the
cumulative last one matters, resolved the same way a real shell would,
one `cd` per flag in order), or failing that the last `cd <dir>` seen
in command position before the invocation, falling back to the hook
payload's cwd when neither is present. The command-position and
destination-ref regexes are both extended to recognize one or more
`-C <dir>` global flags between `git` and `push`, so a `-C`-redirected
invocation is no longer invisible to classification at all -- it was
previously skipped by both checks outright.

Ordinary `cd`-containing compound commands that never reach a `git
push` are completely unaffected: the cd-scanning logic only runs once
the command-position check has already confirmed a real push invocation
is present, so this never denies "every command that contains cd."

Also added two fail-closed cases per review: if the resolved directory
cannot be entered, or `git branch --show-current` returns empty there
(not a repository, or a detached HEAD), the hook now denies with a
reason naming that the branch could not be determined, rather than
falling through and allowing. This is the central fix -- the old
behavior (empty branch reads as "not main/master," so allow) was
exactly the silent-allow failure mode every other fix in this mission
exists to close.

Ten new test cases (five scenarios x jq/no-jq): a -C-redirected push to
the main checkout from a feature-worktree cwd (deny), the mirror case
redirected to a feature worktree from the main checkout's cwd (allow),
the same redirection via a preceding cd (deny), a payload cwd naming a
real but non-repository directory with a plain push (deny, fail
closed), and a detached-HEAD repository with a plain push (deny, fail
closed). The non-repository fixture is built with `env -u TMPDIR
mktemp -d` specifically to land outside this checkout's own working
tree -- TMPDIR for this whole suite is this repo's own .tmp/, so a
plain subdirectory of the shared WORKDIR has no .git of its own but
still sits inside this repo's tree, and `git branch --show-current`
would silently walk past it to this repo's own branch instead of
failing the way a genuinely isolated directory does. One existing case
(the compound-command-with-cd test) was adjusted to `cd` into a real
subdirectory of the worktree instead of a nonexistent one, since F5's
resolution step now makes that `cd` target meaningful rather than
inert. 40 cases total, 0 failures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
)" 2>&1
